user.title: Battery Opt
user.description: Prices come from Home Assistant's own OMIE integration - set it up first (Settings > Devices & services > Add > OMIE). The marstek_modbus entities are optional until the battery arrives: leave all four empty for planning-only mode (plans and savings are computed, nothing actuates). Note: force_mode, rs485_control_mode, set_charge_power and charge_to_soc ship disabled by default in the Marstek integration - enable them first (user_work_mode is enabled by default). The charge-to-SoC and cutoff numbers are optional extras; the cutoff numbers do not exist on the Venus E V3, so leave them empty there - the reserve floor is the battery's to manage. The load and grid-import sensors are also optional - everything degrades gracefully (flat load forecast, cost sensor unavailable) until they are set.

data.load_sensor: House load sensor (power W or energy kWh, optional)
data.grid_power_sensor: Grid import power sensor (W, charge-power loop)
data.dry_run: Dry-run (Task 12): keep actuating the static plan; the greedy stays advisory. Disable only after Checkpoint C

error.omie_not_set_up: The OMIE integration is not set up. Add it first: Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > OMIE.
error.battery_entities_all_or_none: Provide all four battery entities (mode, charge power, external-control switch, work mode), or none of them (planning-only mode until the battery arrives).
error.timezone_not_lisbon: Home Assistant's timezone must be Europe/Lisbon: the tariff calendar, the OMIE market day and every trigger are Portugal-local. Change it under Settings > System > General.
